blocks.content: A Judge of the Supreme Court shall not be removed from his office except by an order of the President passed after an address by each House of Parliament supported by a majority of the total membership of that House and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members of that House present and voting.

items: High Court judges submit their resignation to the President of India, NOT to the Governor of the state.
Members of State Public Service Commissions are appointed by the Governor, but their removal power lies exclusively with the President of India.
Grounds for impeachment of SC/HC judges are limited strictly to 'proved misbehaviour' or 'incapacity' under Article 124(4).
CAG, CEC, and UPSC Chairmen share the same removal process and grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Supreme Court judges hold office until the age of 65 years and submit their resignation directly to the President of India.
High Court judges hold office until attaining 62 years of age and can be removed by the President through a parliamentary address.
The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) and Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) share the same tenure of 6 years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.
Members of the State Public Service Commission (SPSC) are appointed by the Governor but can only be removed by the President of India.
Removal of Judges requires a special majority in both Houses of Parliament on grounds of 'proved misbehaviour' or 'incapacity'.
